utterances.text: Now, in this -- in this video, we see Martic say that: "We had a blessing from 99 per cent of you and that you were convinced that we could complete our task given to us by our president of the Republic of Srpska Krajina, Mr. Goran Hadzic, and by the government of Republika Srpska Krajina." Now, my question is, coming back now, you said a decision was made to attempt this breakthrough. Who made decision in Knin on that point, if you know?

utterances.speaker: VELJKO DZAKULA [Resumed]
utterances.text: That decision was made by the president of the republic, as well as the government of the RSK, I believe.

utterances.speaker: MR. STRINGER
utterances.text: Thank you. Now, my last couple of questions, Mr. Dzakula, relates to something you testified about yesterday at page 513 of the transcript. You were talking about your conversations with Mr. Zecevic when you were travelling to and from New York, your conversations about the refugee issue. Do you remember that?

utterances.speaker: VELJKO DZAKULA [Resumed]
utterances.text: I do.

utterances.speaker: MR. STRINGER
utterances.text: And this is page 513, line 6. Yesterday you said: "After our conversations to New York and back, he told Goran Hadzic that I was in favour of cohabitation with the Croats. No one else could have. So I was closely observed in terms of what I was to say." Do you remember that testimony?

utterances.speaker: VELJKO DZAKULA [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, I do recall that.

utterances.speaker: MR. STRINGER
utterances.text: Now, my question is: Why did you conclude that it was Mr. Zecevic who said this, who told this to Goran Hadzic?

utterances.speaker: VELJKO DZAKULA [Resumed]
utterances.text: Because he disagreed with my position. He denied it. He said that he understood it to be the wish of the people but that he was unable and unwilling to accept it. If he was unable to accept my words as such, it would be realistic of me to expect that it -- he was the only person who could say such a thing. My colleagues in Western Slavonia did not have such an opportunity, and their position was similar to mine. At that time, I had not spoken with anyone from the government on that topic.

utterances.speaker: MR. STRINGER
utterances.text: And what was the time-frame of these trips to New York with Mr. Zecevic you're talking about, month and year?

utterances.speaker: VELJKO DZAKULA [Resumed]
utterances.text: I think it was in late March 1992.

utterances.speaker: MR. STRINGER
utterances.text: And you've said here that he told Goran Hadzic that you were in favour of cohabitation with the Croats. Did you ever get any reaction from Mr. Hadzic about that?

utterances.speaker: VELJKO DZAKULA [Resumed]
utterances.text: When he summoned me to discuss things with me and when he asked me about it, I could feel in his voice --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE DELVOIE
utterances.text: Just a moment.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZIVANOVIC
utterances.text: It was not subject of cross-examination in the last question.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE DELVOIE
utterances.text: Mr. Stringer.

utterances.speaker: MR. STRINGER
utterances.text: Well, I think this falls within the scope of the cross-examination. These are -- this all -- I'm looking at again page 513 of yesterday's transcript. Counsel was asking the witness about these conversations. He raised the conversations with Mr. Zecevic in his cross-examination, that these conversations occurred during their trips to New York. And then during that, the witness said that he told Goran Hadzic, Mr. Zecevic. I think it's a fair and logical next question to ask whether that resulted in any reaction. It's --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE DELVOIE
utterances.text: Objection overruled.

utterances.speaker: MR. STRINGER
utterances.text: Would you like me to repeat the question, Mr. Dzakula?

utterances.speaker: VELJKO DZAKULA [Resumed]
utterances.text: No. I remember the question. When Mr. Hadzic asked me about whether I was in favour of cohabitation with Croats, he put a stress on it, something along the lines: How can you even think of such situation? Could you even have said that? And I'm asking you, because I will believe what you tell me. From that, I understood that he did not support that thesis.

utterances.speaker: MR. STRINGER
utterances.text: Now, this conversation with Mr. Hadzic, when did this -- when did this occur? Is this something you've testified about before?

utterances.speaker: VELJKO DZAKULA [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, I have, in some previous cases. I think it was in late April or early May 1992.

utterances.speaker: MR. STRINGER
utterances.text: Do you know where that conversation occurred?

utterances.speaker: VELJKO DZAKULA [Resumed]
utterances.text: There was a government session in Erdut. There I was summoned to his office.

utterances.speaker: MR. STRINGER
utterances.text: Was anyone else present?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE DELVOIE
utterances.text: Mr. Zivanovic.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZIVANOVIC
utterances.text: May I have any reference in my cross-examination about this subject, please.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE DELVOIE
utterances.text: I seem to remember that I overruled your objection. Aren't you repeating the objection?

utterances.speaker: MR. ZIVANOVIC
utterances.text: No, Your Honours. I cannot follow this part of my cross-examination. There is no -- I cannot find it.

utterances.speaker: MR. STRINGER
utterances.text: Well --

utterances.speaker: MR. ZIVANOVIC
utterances.text: I'd just like to see a reference. It is not an objection.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE DELVOIE
utterances.text: All right. Sorry. Mr. Stringer.

utterances.speaker: MR. STRINGER
utterances.text: Our position, Mr. President, is that this flows logically from the question raised in cross-examination, the answers that were given in cross about conversations with Zecevic that were then conveyed to Mr. Hadzic. I think it's a fair continuation of what was raised during the cross.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE DELVOIE
utterances.text: Within limits, Mr. Stringer.

utterances.speaker: MR. STRINGER
utterances.text: I'll just -- yes, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: MR. STRINGER
utterances.text: You mentioned the government session in Erdut where you were summoned to his office, and I asked whether anyone else was present. If you can just answer that question and then we'll see whether that's sufficient.

utterances.speaker: VELJKO DZAKULA [Resumed]
utterances.text: It -- next to Goran Hadzic, there was Zeljko Raznjatovic, Arkan.

utterances.speaker: MR. STRINGER
utterances.text: Mr. President, that completes my redirect. We would tender into evidence the video 4945.2, which was just shown.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE DELVOIE
utterances.text: Admitted and marked.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: It shall be assigned Exhibit P48. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE DELVOIE
utterances.text: The other -- the other documents tendered.

utterances.speaker: MR. STRINGER
utterances.text: The Croatian intelligence report we are not tendering.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE DELVOIE
utterances.text: Okay. Thank you very much.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE DELVOIE
utterances.text: Two videos. Two videos, Mr. Stringer, were shown, and only one tendered.

utterances.speaker: MR. STRINGER
utterances.text: My apologies. Both being tendered, 4842.1 and 4945.2.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE DELVOIE
utterances.text: Admitted and marked.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: Your Honours, 65 ter document 4842.1 shall be assigned Exhibit P49. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE DELVOIE
utterances.text: Anything coming out of redirect from Defence?

utterances.speaker: MR. ZIVANOVIC
utterances.text: No, Your Honour. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE DELVOIE
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE DELVOIE
utterances.text: Mr. Dzakula, this brings us to the end of your testimony. I thank you for coming to the Tribunal to assist us with your testimony. You are now released as a witness. The usher will escort you out of the courtroom, and we wish you a safe journey home. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you, Your Honour, and I wish you a pleasant stay here.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE DELVOIE
utterances.text: We take the adjournment to Tuesday afternoon, 1.30, in this courtroom. I wish all of you a good weekend. Court adjourned.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE DELVOIE
utterances.text: to be reconvened on Tuesday, the 30th day of October, 2012, at 1.30 p.m. 25

procedural_notes.text: --- Whereupon the hearing adjourned at 12.01 p.m.,
